OpenELIS Global Phase 5 Admin Redesign Finalization v2.0

The admin plan versus the running app

Phase 5 was scoped in April against a 42-page admin inventory. Three months of development have moved underneath it. This is every admin page in OpenELIS, walked route by route on the live instance, with a finalized disposition for each.

01 Where the work actually stands

Forty-five admin pages exist today. Twenty-one of them need no design work at all — they shipped while the plan sat at its approval gate.

Phase 5b

Ten pages need genuine design work — not the 42 the roadmap projected. Revised estimate: roughly 10 sessions against the original ~30.

The plan is not slightly stale — it is structurally stale. Nine pages scheduled for design have already shipped. Five pages scheduled for redesign contain zero configuration rows. Eleven pages exist that the roadmap has never heard of. Two of the five "Top-5 priority" pages are already modern Carbon screens.

05 Four decisions I need from you

Q1 The two thin Workflow Tuning pages

Validation Configuration has 4 charset properties; WorkPlan Configuration has 3. Both are too small to justify a page, but F2 rules out a tab-based settings page.

  • Keep both as minimal pages in Workflow Tuning — consistent with F2, but two very sparse screens.
  • Fold both into the Application Properties redesign as domain-grouped sections. Same SystemConfiguration rows, one surface — grouping, not tabs, so F2 holds. Recommended.
  • Fold the charsets into Application Properties; keep WorkPlan where it is, since its settings are workflow-facing.

Q2 Test Management

A ~22-link legacy hub whose links now largely duplicate the shipped Test Catalogue Editor. Redesign it as a modern landing page, or retire it and redistribute the genuinely unique links — spelling corrections, batch renames, Compliance Standards?

  • Recommendation: retire. It is the last big JSP doorway and the editor has superseded most of it.

Q3 Role Management

The RBAC PRD is from March and has not shipped. Does it stay in Phase 5 as the one real People & Access gap, or move to its own track given its size?

Q4 Defect handling

L-01 (Language Management hard delete) is a live MUST-D violation; L-02 (blank eqaProgram) is a live broken route. File these as bugs now, independent of the redesign, or fold them into the redesign tickets?

Plus two finished specs awaiting delivery: Program Entry (OGC-781) and Feature Flags.

08 What users will hate

The adversarial pass, ranked by pain. Several of these are criticisms of the sections above — including one that undercuts a decision I locked in §03.

The correction first. F3 retired five pages because they showed zero rows on testing.openelis-global.org. One dev instance is not evidence that a production deployment has nothing configured there — these are SystemConfiguration rows filtered by category, and Result Entry Configuration is especially suspect since the audit raised C045/C046 against it, implying it had content when audited.

The demo instance proves the general point. demo.openelis-global.org runs 3.2.1.9 branded "Labsolution", and its admin nav is materially different: Barcode Configuration where testing has Label Presets, and no Vector Surveillance, no Sample Acceptance Checklist, no Test Catalogue Management group at all. The 45-page inventory is one build's inventory, not the product's. Retiring a page a deployment uses is a data-access regression discovered during an accreditation audit.

01 The URL migration is scoped as routing. It is a documentation migration.

docs-manual/contracts.json pins each manual section to live routes and on-load UI anchors, and a drift check asserts them. Every admin manual section breaks twice on migration day: the pinned route moves, and the screenshots show a dead breadcrumb. Contracts are already at capturedVersion 3.2.1.10 against a live 3.2.2.0 — the manual drifts before we touch anything. Outside the repo nothing redirects at all: locally-authored French training decks, two years of deep links in Jira and Slack, and support muscle memory. /analyze Pass N exists to catch exactly this and I ran it without flagging one docs impact.

02 Forty-five pages get reorganized and there is no search

The shell brief defers cross-bucket search to "Phase 6 if admins ask for it." That is backwards — search is what makes a reorganization survivable. On day one every admin's spatial memory is void and the only recovery path is browsing 12 lopsided buckets (System Administration holds 8 pages; Reference Data holds 1).

03 The half-migrated state is the steady state

Story A wraps legacy JSP pages in the new Carbon shell — a Carbon breadcrumb and rail around a 2009 form. With 10 pages still needing design, that mixed state persists for many releases. It is not a brief awkward window, and it reads as less finished than either UI alone.

04 The Application Properties redesign may hurt its heaviest users

61 raw keys in a flat list is bad for a newcomer but has one real virtue: Ctrl+F finds anything. Group them into ~14 cards and an admin who knows login.saml.entityId must now know which card owns it. The heaviest users are implementers and support who already know the key names — grouping optimizes for the once-a-year visitor and taxes the weekly one.

05 Francophone deployments get a more English admin

Live Translation Management reports French at 1257/2003 — 62.8%, 746 strings already missing. This plan adds 12 bucket names, 45 page titles, every breadcrumb and every retirement notice. t(key, fallback) guarantees a key, not a translation — the fallback is the English string. Madagascar and Côte d'Ivoire use admin heavily and would see more English than they do today.

06 Menu Configuration risks ceremony without confidence

If the redesign paginates the ~300-node tree per scope, an admin making a bulk change now saves five times instead of once — and still cannot see what they changed before committing.

07 There is no transition plan, and retirement notices dead-end

No flag, no opt-in period, no "old nav still available", no in-app "this moved" affordance. And a notice that says this page has moved to an admin hunting for results on workplan tells them their setting is gone and offers nothing further.

08 The uncomfortable question — who asked for this?

Nothing in the Phase 5 corpus cites user research. The 74 audit findings are an expert critique, not user demand. Meanwhile Program Entry is still a raw "Edit Json" textarea in production with a finished, approved, unshipped v2 spec. That is a page where admins demonstrably struggle — while the plan proposes ~10 sessions plus a large routing migration to reorganize pages that mostly work.

And one sequencing change, which is the most important line here. Before Story A gets a ticket: ship the two finished specs — Program Entry and Feature Flags — and put the IA migration behind five to ten admin conversations at two deployments. If admins report they can't find things, the reorganization is justified and we learn which buckets are wrong. If they report that Application Properties and Program Entry are the pain, we have saved most of the program's cost and delivered the part that mattered.
